\label{lemma-characterize-reduced}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is reduced, see
Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-reduced}.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$
such that each $\Gamma(U_i, \mathcal{O}_X)$ is reduced.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring
$\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is reduced.
\item For every open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is reduced.
\end{enumerate}
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 196 lists four equivalent conditions for reducedness of X, including existence of reduced affine cover and reduced section rings over every affine/all opens. All four equivalent conditions and the quantifier distinctions are preserved.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-irreducible}
Let $X$ be a scheme.
The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is irreducible.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$
such that $I$ is not empty, $U_i$ is irreducible for all $i \in I$, and
$U_i \cap U_j \not = \emptyset$ for all $i, j \in I$.
\item The scheme $X$ is nonempty and every nonempty affine open
$U \subset X$ is irreducible.
\end{enumerate}
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 216 equates irreducibility of X with an explicitly nonempty affine cover by pairwise-intersecting irreducible affines and with nonempty X whose every nonempty affine open is irreducible. All nonempty qualifiers are retained.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-integral}
A scheme $X$ is integral if and only if it is reduced and irreducible.
stage_b_review_note: Pinned lemma 259 characterizes integral schemes by reduced AND irreducible. The draft keeps the two-way implication and the conjunction.
statement: A scheme $X$ is integral if and only if it is reduced and irreducible.
conclusions: $X$ is integral if and only if it is reduced and irreducible.
